MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 25, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR MITCHELL at 7:02 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Boy Scout Troop 378 members Matt Yang and Josh Ikagami led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Zuckerman
City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT “RECYCLING HERO” DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF FREE
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE – SECOND QUARTER 2019

  RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 31 SANTA BELLA ROAD
  COMMERCIAL WINNER: THE GENERAL STORE

Waste Management presented retiring City Manager Prichard with a commemorative manure
waste collection bin in recognition of his service to the City.

B.  RESOLUTION OF COMMENDATION – DOUGLAS R. PRICHARD, RETIRING CITY
  MANAGER

MAYOR MITCHELL presented a Resolution of Commendation to Doug Prichard in recognition
of his 34 years of dedicated service to the City of Rolling Hills Estates.

Mr. Prichard was also recognized for his service by Aurelia Freidman on behalf of Congressman
Ted Lieu; Mayor Pro Tem John Cruikshank, Rancho Palos Verdes; Council Member Patrick

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JUNE 25, 2019
 Wilson, Rolling Hills; Board President Linda Reid, PVPUSD; and Jon Shull, Chief Executive
Officer, California JPIA.

City Manager Prichard thanked the City Council, staff and members of the community for their
support over the years and expressed his sincere appreciation for having been given the
opportunity to serve this community for the last 34 years.

MAYOR MITCHELL announced that Item 12A will be taken out of order and that Item 2 regarding
the First Amendment to the City Manager Employment will be tabled until all City Council
Members are present.

MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

A.  CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Appoint Greg Grammer City Manager
  effective as of July 9, 2019 and approve the execution of the City Manager Employment
  Agreement; and 2) Adopt the First Amendment to the City Manager Employment
  Agreement providing for PARS longevity deferred compensation contributions by the City
  on behalf of Mr. Grammer at an amount equal for five percent (5%) of his annual base
  salary effective July 9, 2019 through June 30, 2020.

  City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the provision for a PARS
  contribution, MAYOR MITCHELL explained that discussion on that matter will be tabled
  until all council members are present.

  City Attorney Davis further clarified that the employment agreement does not include the
  PARS contribution.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPOINT GREG GRAMMER CITY MANAGER
  EFFECTIVE JULY 9, 2019 AND APPROVE EXECUTION OF THE CITY
  MANAGER EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

Assistant City Manager Grammer thanked the members of the City Council for their trust and
support and stated that he is honored and humbled to be given this opportunity. He thanked
retiring City Manager Prichard for his leadership, mentorship and friendship and expressed his
appreciation for City staff. He recognized his parents and his partner and thanked them for their
support. Finally, he thanked the residents of Rolling Hills Estates for their support and for being
active and involved in preserving the unique character of the community.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JUNE 25, 2019
 Council Member Zuckerman thanked retiring City Manager for his service and expressed his
sincere appreciation for his attention to detail and keen awareness.

Council Member Huff expressed her appreciation for retiring City Manager Prichard’s leadership
and guidance and thanked him for his service to the community.

The City Council recessed to a brief reception honoring retiring City Manager Doug Prichard.

MAYOR MITCHELL called the meeting back to order at 8:15 p.m. with Council Members Huff
and Zuckerman in attendance.

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council.
  There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote.
  (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on separately.)

  MAYOR MITCHELL requested that Item 5K be removed for individual consideration.

  There being no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-J AS
  PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 11, 2019

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS JUNE 2019

  APPROVED WARRANTS 61568 THROUGH 61630 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $346,418.95 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 060119 THROUGH 060319 IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $107,944.29 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF
  $454,363.24 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT MAY 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED

JUNE 25, 2019

  DIRECTOR,  PLANNING  MANAGER  AND  ADMINISTRATIVE AIDE JOB
  CLASSIFICATION, DESCRIPTION AND RESPECTIVE PAY RANGE

  ADOPTED AS PRESENTED

J.  2019-20 MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING – ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  EMPLOYEES’ ASSOCIATION

City Manager Prichard read Resolution 2441 by title.

REMOVED FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION:

K.  SALARY RESOLUTIONS FY 2019-20:

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolutions 2442, 2443, 2444, 2445 and
  2446 authorizing the number and compensation of employees within City Service.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per the agenda material). He stated that
  given the earlier discussion regarding the PARS contribution and the COUNCIL’S desire
  to table consideration of that matter until all council members are present, COUNCIL
  could make the necessary amendments related to the PARS contribution and act
  individually on these Resolutions

  MAYOR MITCHELL commented that the two resolutions that include a provision for the
  PARS contribution are Resolution 2444 and 2446.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JUNE 25, 2019
   Following brief discussion, the following actions were taken:

  RESOLUTION NO. 2442 – CLASSIFIED EMPLOYEE GROUP

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2442 – CLASSIFIED

City Manager Prichard read Resolution 2444 by title.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JUNE 25, 2019
   RESOLUTION NO. 2445 – PART-TIME EMPLOYEE GROUP

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2445 – PART-TIME
  EMPLOYEE GROUP AS PRESENTED

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Manager Prichard read Resolution 2445 by title.

  RESOLUTION NO. 2446 – CITY MANAGER CLASSIFICATION

  MAYOR MITCHELL commented that Section 3 of this resolution contains a provision for a

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,

  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Manager Prichard read Resolution 2446 by title.

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

A.  FY 2019-20 BUDGET PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPTION:

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Open the Public Hearing and take public
  testimony related to budget adoption including: appropriation limit, fees and charges, fund
  balance policy and investment policy; 2) Close the Public Hearing; and 3) Review and
  approve Resolution 2438 – Adopting the consolidated Budget; Resolution 2439 –
  Establishing the 2019-20 Appropriation Limit; Resolution 2440 – Establishing Schedule
  of Municipal Fees & Charges; Statement of Fund Balance Policy and Statement of
  Investment Policy.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
JUNE 25, 2019
   City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per the agenda material). He noted that
  the pages left intentionally blank will be replaced with a standalone budget summary
  document as recommended at the Budget Study Session.

  MAYOR MITCHELL declared the public hearing open and called for public comment.
  Hearing no one, the public hearing was closed.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead stated that the budget summary document will be provided to the COUNCIL

  Following brief discussion, the following actions were taken:

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION 2440 ESTABLISHING THE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
JUNE 25, 2019

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT THE STATEMENT OF FUND BALANCE
  POLICY AND STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY AS PRESENTED.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

NEW BUSINESS

A.  RESOLUTION NO. 2437 – CONGESTION MANAGEMENT PROGRAM (CMP) OPT-OUT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Resolution 2437 electing to be exempt
  from the Congestion Management Program in accordance with CMP State statue.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  confirmed that there would be no negative implications if the City decided not to opt-out.
  Given that fact, COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that he would recommended
  not opting out or taking no action because he believes this action puts regional interests
  ahead of local interests. He further commented that he believes addressing congestion
  at the local level is an important consideration and it is important to focus on levels of
  service at the local level as compared to vehicle miles traveled.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer commented that this program has been suspended for
  a number of years and included a very cumbersome reporting requirement that didn’t
  really accomplish anything.

  MAYOR MITCHELL commented that she would recommend that the City join the cities
  that are opting out and adopt this resolution.

  Following brief discussion,

  MAYOR MITCHELL moved, seconded by, COUNCILMEMBER HUFF

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION 2437 ELECTING TO BE
  EXEMPT FROM THE CONGESTION MANAGEMENT PROGRAM IN
  ACCORDANCE WITH CMP STATE STATUTE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell
  NOES:  Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Manager Prichard read Resolution 2437 by title.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8
JUNE 25, 2019
 B.  APPROVAL OF A FIVE-YEAR MUNICIPAL LAW ENFORCEMENT SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt the Five-Year Municipal Law Enforcement
  Services Agreement by and between the County of Los Angeles and the City of Rolling
  Hills Estates as presented.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  In response to MAYOR MITCHELL regarding the increase in cost, Assistant City Manager
  Grammer stated that this year’s increase is approximately 4%. City Manager Prichard
  stated that the Service Level Authorization Form (Form 575) sets the rates provided for
  in the agreement and it will be updated and approved each year of the five year
  agreement.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF regarding the potential for unforeseen future
  rate increases, City Manager Prichard stated that the City could look for other options for
  policing services or adjust service levels as needed.

  CITY ATTORNEY DAVIS further clarified that the agreement provides an option for
  withdrawal when there is a notice of rate increase.

  Brief discussion ensued concerning the agreement specifically regarding the section on
  indemnification.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE FIVE-YEAR MUNICIPAL LAW
  ENFORCEMENT SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH THE COUNTY OF LOS
  ANGELES.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

NONE.

appreciation for his professionalism.

meeting including concern expressed by the equestrian community regarding the delays and

Thursday, June 27, 2019 at 6:00 p.m. at which time COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF will be recognized
for her service as Chair of the Board.

MAYOR MITCHELL noted that the Sanitation District Collective Committee is scheduled to meet
on Wednesday, June 26 to vote on a proposed labor agreement but she is unable to attend the
